The Invesco KBW Bank ETF (NASDAQ:KBWB) trades near $87, about 14% below its August record. Investors who bought KBWB saw this drop while bank profits kept growing.

Who is Danny / Shutterstock.com

Truist Securities analyst Brian Foran said financials posted their worst month against the S&P 500 since 1990. The KBW Nasdaq Bank Index is down 13% from mid-August.

KBWB fell 8% in the past month. It remains up 5% this year and 15% over twelve months, ahead of the S&P 500's 14%.

Foran compared the pattern to the dot-com era, when money flowed into technology and financials fell behind. The selloff looks like rotation driven by fund flows rather than by bank results.

Profits Keep Climbing While Prices Slide

JPMorgan Chase (NYSE:JPM) earned an adjusted $6.14 per share in the second quarter, up 13%, according to Truist Securities. Bank of America (NYSE:BAC) grew net income 28%, and Citigroup (NYSE:C) raised first-quarter EPS to $3.06 from $1.96.

JPM Earnings Explorer — 24/7 Wall St.
Margins, Credit and Shrinking Deal Fees

Net interest margin is the gap between what a bank pays depositors and what it earns on loans. The 10-year to 2-year Treasury spread is 0.46%, down from 0.74% in February. That gap gets squeezed when the curve flattens.

Credit quality is back in question. Citigroup set aside an extra $597 million in reserves due to economic uncertainty, though credit card delinquencies fell to 2.85%.

title: Bank of America Raises Long-Term Copper Forecast to $12,000 Per Ton
detail:
Bank of America Raises Long-Term Copper Forecast to $12,000 Per Ton
Fiona Craig
Fri, October 2, 2026 at 9:27 AM EDT
BAC
ALI=F
HG=F
Trade BAC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Copper wire ©Adobe Stock Images

Bank of America has raised its long-term copper price forecast by 20% to $12,000 per ton, equivalent to $5.44 per pound in 2026 dollars, according to a commodities strategy update from the bank.

The strategists attributed the revised forecast primarily to continuing supply constraints, which they said have contributed to copper's recent price performance.

The adjustment follows more than a year of policy developments and other market events that have affected the commodities outlook. Bank of America also pointed to the continuing potential for volatility related to the conflict in the Middle East.

The bank identified several factors that could affect its copper outlook, including the possibility of an energy-related shock to demand and a pause in capital expenditure on data centres.

Bank of America made relatively limited changes elsewhere in its commodities forecasts. The bank lowered its 2027 aluminium price estimate by 5% to $3,625 per ton.

For gold, the strategists said higher interest rates and a stronger US dollar were creating a bearish price backdrop.

Gil Luria raised MU's price target to $2,100, which stands as Wall Street's highest, implying 91% upside after shares already surged 503% over the past year.

Goldman Sachs holds MU at $1,100 while Bank of America projects annual buybacks of between $60 billion and $100 billion by fiscal 2028, making cash returns the stronger bull argument.

The bull case collapses if Q1 revenue misses the $61.5 billion guide, no buyback authorization arrives by December 9, or quarterly guidance stops rising.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

Gil Luria of DA Davidson raised his price target to $2,100 from $2,000, the highest on the Street, and maintained a Buy rating after Micron Technology's (NASDAQ:MU) September 30, 2026 earnings report. Rosenblatt also raised its target to $1,900 from $1,500.

Shutterstock

The stock rose 3.03% on October 1 and closed at $1,097.39. From that close, the new target implies about 91% upside.

The shares have gained 503.44% over the past year and 284.73% in 2026, according to DA Davidson. For the price to nearly double again, memory prices would have to stay tight longer than in any earlier cycle.

Which Half of the $2,100 Target Does the Work, according to DA Davidson

Luria applies 13 times to calendar 2027 earnings. For a semiconductor stock, that multiple is low. The assumption is that pricing holds near peak levels well into 2027.

Luria points to 26 long-term supply agreements and says memory markets "could be even tighter in 2028 than they are today." These agreements turn commodity sales into contracted volume on a take-or-pay basis, supporting roughly $150 billion in remaining performance obligations.

Results That Explain the Optimism

Fiscal fourth-quarter revenue reached $54.23 billion, up 379%, and adjusted EPS was $33.42. Guidance calls for $61.5 billion in revenue and $38.15 in EPS next quarter.

MU Earnings Explorer — 24/7 Wall St.

Memory factories cost roughly the same to run regardless of selling price, so most extra revenue becomes profit. Gross margin reached 87%, and the same effect works just as hard when prices fall.

title: IonQ (IONQ) Stock Fair Value Edges Lower After Analysts Rework Growth And Risk
detail:
IonQ (IONQ) Stock Fair Value Edges Lower After Analysts Rework Growth And Risk
Bailey Pemberton
Fri, October 2, 2026 at 1:09 AM EDT
IONQ
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

IonQ's updated framework now points to a fair value of US$66.63, trimmed from US$68.41. This gives you a fresh reference point for how some analysts are thinking about the stock. That reset lines up with recent Street work that tries to balance long term optimism on quantum computing with questions around execution, valuation and timing. As you read on, you will see how this evolving narrative is taking shape and what to watch if you want to follow future shifts in sentiment on IonQ.

Stay updated as the Fair Value for IonQ shifts by adding it to your watchlist or portfolio. Alternatively, explore our Community to discover new perspectives on IonQ.

What Wall Street Has Been Saying
🐂 Bullish Takeaways

Several firms, including BofA and Benchmark, are positive on IonQ as a pure play on quantum computing and see the company as well positioned across computing, communications and sensing use cases.

Jefferies and Morgan Stanley highlight progress on IonQ's roadmap and Tempo deployments, with comments around manufacturability, scalability and commercial traction following recent results and investor events.

Wedbush and B. Riley point to the broader quantum sector setup and describe IonQ as a leading platform, with B. Riley outlining a potential path to US$1b in annualized revenue along with possible inorganic growth.

The SkyWater Technology partnership is cited by Jefferies as already helping IonQ shorten hardware cycle times, which analysts view as helpful for execution on its qubit scaling plans.

🐻 Bearish Takeaways

Some optimism is tempered by valuation and execution questions, with Mizuho trimming its IonQ price target from US$61 to US$52 and Jefferies reducing its target from US$85 to US$75 even while keeping positive ratings.

Wedbush stresses that there is still no clear winning quantum modality, which leaves IonQ exposed to technology risk if industry standards or preferred architectures evolve differently over time.

Do your thoughts align with the Bull or Bear Analysts? Perhaps you think there's more to the story. Head to the Simply Wall St Community to discover more perspectives!

NYSE:IONQ 1-Year Stock Price Chart

How This Changes the Fair Value For IonQ

Fair Value has been adjusted to US$66.63 from US$68.41 in the updated framework for IonQ.

Revenue Growth assumptions are set at 71.56%, compared with the previous 55.27% figure.

Net Profit Margin expectations are now 20.07%, up from 7.63% in the prior model.

The future P/E multiple has been reduced to about 171x from about 747x.

The Discount Rate applied in the model is now 11.26%, compared with 8.49% previously.
